ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with center P. Points Q and S lie on the circle on the right side, and QS is a vertical chord. Point R lies on chord QS, and segment PR goes from the center P to the chord. The right-angle mark at R shows PR is perpendicular to QS. The given text says the radius of circle P is 5 and PR = 3. Reasoning: Since a perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, R is the midpoint of QS, so QS = 2·RS. In right triangle PRS, PS is a radius, so PS = 5, and PR = 3. By the Pythagorean theorem, RS = sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = sqrt(25 - 9) = sqrt(16) = 4. Therefore QS = 2·4 = 8.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing a vertical chord QS of circle centered at P, with PR perpendicular to QS and R lying on the chord. From the text, the circle has radius 5 and the distance from the center P to the chord line is PR=3. Set up coordinates with P=(0,0) and PR along the positive x-axis, so the chord QS lies on the vertical line x=3. The circle equation is x^2+y^2=25. Intersections with x=3 satisfy 9+y^2=25, so y=±4. Thus the chord extends from y=4 to y=-4, giving QS=4-(-4)=8.
